question: I heard the GI Bill doesn't work for trade school. Is that true?

answer: No, that isn't true. Depending on the benefit you're eligible for, GI Bill education benefits can pay for vocational and technical training, non-college degree programs, apprenticeships and on-the-job training, licensing and certification tests, and flight training [D21]. The catch is that the school or program must be approved for VA benefits. question: I was in Iraq in 2007 around burn pits. Can I get VA health care?

answer: Probably worth applying. Most veterans discharged under conditions other than dishonorable can apply for VA health care, and your honorable discharge meets that [D08]. Iraq is among the locations where burn pit exposure may have occurred [D09]. You can use the VA.gov screening tools to check eligibility, and you can apply at any time online at VA.gov, by phone, by mail, or in person at a VA medical center [D09][D08].
